subject: parser warning of non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable when using matrix head / col

messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: parser warning of non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable when using matrix head / col
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to estimate forecast errors with a t-distribution for multiple forecasters with different forecast history (but common prior).

STAN code as follow:
 
data {
  // common prior
  real f_s_l;  // prior for sigma location
  real f_s_s;  // prior for sigma scale   

  int<lower=1> f_N_a;  // num of forecasters
  int<lower=1> f_N_h;  // max hist depth

  int f_analyst_hist_depth [f_N_a];      // depth of hist for each forecaster
  matrix[f_N_h, f_N_a] f_hist_actual;    // historical actual (hist (r) x forecaster (c))
  matrix[f_N_h, f_N_a] f_hist_forecast;  // historical actual (hist (r) x forecaster (c))

  vector[f_N_a] f_forecast_new;          // new forecasts supplied
}

parameters {
  vector<lower=0>[f_N_a] f_sigma;      
}

model {
  for (a in 1:f_N_a) {

    f_sigma[a] ~ cauchy (f_s_l, f_s_l);

    /*
     * decode matrix as follow:
     * select by row_ID (per analyst) -> vector
     * from the vector -> select appropriate hist_depth
     */
    for (d in 1:f_analyst_hist_depth[a]) {
      f_hist_actual[d, a] ~ student_t (f_analyst_hist_depth[a]-1,
                       f_hist_forecast[d, a],
                       f_sigma[a]);

                       }
}

This runs ok. But, then I think I can optimize the inner for-loop with vectorization.

New mode section:
model {
  for (a in 1:f_N_a) {

    f_sigma[a] ~ cauchy (f_s_l, f_s_l);

    head (col(f_hist_actual, a), f_analyst_hist_depth[a]) ~ student_t (f_analyst_hist_depth[a]-1,
                                       head (col(f_hist_forecast, a), f_analyst_hist_depth[a]),
                                           f_sigma[a]);

  }
}

However, I got a parser warning:

TRANSLATING MODEL 't6' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
 You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
  Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
    col(f_hist_actual,a) ~ student_t_log(...)


I'm a quite new to STAN and Bayesian stats, but, I am at lost in why either head or col function would contain non-linear transform?

Many thanks

Andy
